sentences.text: The single well-known species, P. anglicus, measured about 25 centimeters in length.
Its braincase is one of only two such structures ever found for this rare group of fish.
This preserved part of the skull offers valuable clues about early vertebrate evolution.
Most fossils come from Old Red Sandstone layers in the United Kingdom.
Two other uncertain species were identified from shoulder bones found in Herefordshire and Ukraine.
Scientists place Ptomacanthus within the larger group Chondrichthyes.
These fish lived during the Lochkovian stage, between 419.62 and 413.02 million years ago.
Finding the braincase sparked renewed arguments about how acanthodians relate to other early vertebrates.
